purpose: Durable chef-facing cover-production contract for Vikings 2026. It separates issue-specific cover composition from series-wide trade-dress authority, fixes the municipal-publication shell across the run, requires actual pixel inspection of canonical identity references, and preserves a deliberately different graphic architecture for each issue.

authority.issueRecipe: The exact assembled Vikings cover recipe controls the issue-specific selling image, cast, environment, composition, spoiler ceiling, and exact issue lettering for all twelve issues. Issue 1 is production-ready as a painted-comic redraw; its released cover remains authority for trade dress only.
authority.tradeDress: The released Vikings 2026 Issue 1 cover in StarSplitterVisions controls only masthead architecture, publisher badge, VIKINGS 2026! wordmark treatment, year/issue box, horizontal-rule language, issue-strapline placement, top-band proportions, and restrained dark-on-white municipal-publication design.
authority.characterWorld: Released StarSplitterVisions pages plus explicitly approved current-production references control established character identity, faces, bodies, hair, clothing, relative scale, locations, props, rendering language, and later story state. Bjorn and Gunnar may never substitute for one another.
authority.scopeRule: Trade-dress authority does not authorize copying the Issue 1 scene composition into later covers. Later cover images are controlled by their own assembled cover recipes.

canonicalTradeDressReference.requiredUse: pixel-read before every Vikings cover generation
canonicalTradeDressReference.pixelReadRule: Retrieve and inspect the actual local reference pixels in active multimodal context. Repository path, SHA, metadata, prose description, memory, or a statement that the image was previously viewed is not a substitute for current pixel inspection.

observedTradeDress.mastheadField: Large white horizontal field occupying the upper portion of the portrait cover, visually separated from the illustration by dark horizontal rules.
observedTradeDress.publisherBadge: Boxed Star Splitter / VISIONS mark at upper left with star device; year and issue number are contained in the lower portion of the same vertical badge.
observedTradeDress.seriesWordmark: Huge dark condensed all-caps VIKINGS 2026! wordmark spanning the masthead to the right of the publisher badge.
observedTradeDress.issueStrapline: Narrow all-caps line beneath the wordmark, bracketed by thin horizontal rules. For later issues this line carries the issue title.
observedTradeDress.colorLogic: Restrained dark navy/black typography and rules on white masthead; the illustration carries the issue-specific color.
observedTradeDress.letteringRule: Keep the publication architecture stable while changing only issue number and issue strapline. Do not add blurbs, slogans, price bursts, fake barcodes, variant labels, creator credits, or other unscripted promotional copy.
observedTradeDress.compositionRule: The cover illustration begins beneath the masthead. Later issue art should vary boldly by issue while preserving the masthead proportions and overall publication identity.
observedTradeDress.publicationCharacter: Deliberately resembles a boring municipal/public-information publication rather than conventional flashy comic-book branding. Preserve the deadpan civic-document feel; the illustration below provides the visual excitement.

coverRecipeSource.rule: Issue 1 is a dedicated cover recipe. Issues 2–12 use Page 1 of the corresponding normal Vikings issue show and are also addressable through the dedicated Vikings Covers shelf. Use the assembled cover recipe, not raw metadata alone.

mandatoryReferenceGate: Resolve the requested Vikings issue and assemble its exact cover recipe (VIK_S1E01_COVER for Issue 1; VIK_S1E##_P01 for Issues 2–12).

Retrieve and visually inspect the actual pixels of production/references/vikings-2026/assets/covers/issue-01-cover-trade-dress.jpg. Use this released image for trade dress and masthead architecture only, not as authority for the redrawn Issue 1 art or later issue compositions.

Resolve and visually inspect actual released or explicitly approved pixels for every recurring character materially present on the cover. Canonical character identity is absolute; do not reconstruct or average faces from prose.
Use the current issue cover recipe for the hook, cast, graphic architecture, environment, background density, spoiler ceiling, and exact DISPLAY text.
Confirm the cover remains clearly drawn and painted rather than photographic or prestige-TV key art.
Confirm the illustration contains no invented readable environmental writing beyond what the exact cover concept requires.
Confirm the proposed illustration is one dominant issue-specific image, remains legible at thumbnail size, and does not reuse another issue's composition.
Generate only after all applicable visual references are present as pixels in active multimodal context.
coverQualityGate: One-second read: the dominant issue hook is legible immediately.
Thumbnail test: focal silhouette, major shape system, and masthead remain clear when reduced.
Series test: the fixed white municipal-publication masthead unmistakably belongs to Vikings 2026.
Issue test: the image uses its assigned graphic architecture and could not be casually reassigned to another issue.

Style test: clearly drawn and painted comic illustration with controlled texture, expressive faces, believable anatomy and tactile New York surfaces; no photographic skin, lens effects, excessive bokeh, over-rendered fur or cinematic orange/blue grading.
Character test: Bjorn, Gunnar, Astrid and both male Kin match actual canonical reference pixels without substitution, averaging or generic-Viking drift.
Spoiler test: cover promises pressure without revealing the issue's solution, reversal, ruling, or final payoff.
Composition test: no recap collage, generic cast lineup, foreground-commuter filler or repeated ensemble architecture unless the exact issue recipe calls for it.
Lettering test: exact series wordmark, year/issue number and issue strapline only; no invented promotional or environmental text.
Municipal-shell test: the masthead still feels like a dry civic/public-information publication rather than entertainment marketing.
New-York-behavior test: any background people are compositionally useful, sparse when appropriate and routine-driven rather than a gawking audience.

issueLettering.strapline: AT THE MUNICIPAL TEMPORAL DISPLACEMENT INTEGRATION DEPARTMENT

coverLineDoctrine: The masthead/trade dress is intentionally dull, civic and bureaucratic: a white municipal/public-information shell with boxed STAR SPLITTER / VISIONS mark, issue block, enormous condensed VIKINGS 2026! wordmark, thin rules and narrow issue subtitle. Keep it essentially fixed across the run.

The illustration beneath the shell is the sales engine and uses a different graphic architecture for every issue: 1 seated horizontal triptych; 2 steep diagonal ascent; 3 lone figure and large negative space; 4 train/platform split; 5 tight counter transaction; 6 flat institutional symmetry; 7 soaring vertical library volume; 8 low park/picnic composition; 9 circular support-group composition; 10 distributed depth along one neighborhood block; 11 overhead table geometry; 12 dead-center security arch.

The series art is clearly drawn and painted, with controlled texture, expressive faces, believable anatomy and tactile New York environments. Avoid photographic skin, lens effects, over-rendered fur, excessive bokeh and cinematic orange/blue grading.

Canonical character reference pixels are absolute. Bjorn is the close-cropped short-bearded serious leader; Gunnar is the long-haired enormous-bearded navigator with black eye paint. Astrid and both male Kin remain individually recognizable and may not collapse into generic fantasy Vikings.
Do not solve New York indifference by placing foreground commuters around the household. Background people appear only when the composition benefits from them; some covers may have almost none.
Apart from exact required trade dress, readable environmental text generally disappears unless the issue concept requires it. Never invent promotional copy.
Every cover sells one dominant issue-specific contradiction, desire or pressure rather than summarizing the issue.
Spoiler-safe does not mean generic: advertise the loaded problem or desire, but do not visualize the issue's solution, reversal, ruling or final payoff.
issueSequenceRule: Normal Vikings issue assembly order is cover P01 → opening editorial/title splash P02 → story → closing teaser/finale. Covers are not separate from the issue sequence, even though a dedicated cover shelf also exposes the same recipes for focused cover production.
